comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Section 4 constructs square candidates by admissible row permutation and row normalization, while Theorem 1 states distribution-entailment equivalence of the LiNG-D output; it does not assert solvability after a specified intervention.

The published full-law irreducible OICA uniqueness result fixes the source count and projective mixing directions; it does not give the finite source-specific cumulant-order stopping construction or the causal frontier derived here.
The total-effect theorem gives a complete graphical criterion for generic effect identification in acyclic latent-variable LiNGAM.
The cyclic section gives a necessary coefficient-identification condition in general and a complete result for restricted cycle structures.

Theorem 2.3 gives the all-non-Gaussian full-law uniqueness of mixing columns used here. Theorem 1.5 treats the broader at-most-one-Gaussian problem through spans of second Veronese powers, and Algorithm 1 couples second and fourth cumulants, with its first stage recovering non-Gaussian columns from a fourth-order tensor. The present theorem neither strengthens that full-law criterion nor permits Gaussian sources.

Theorem 4a gives essential uniqueness of a three-factor tensor decomposition under the Kruskal-rank inequality; the present theorem verifies that inequality with two degree-\(R_\nu-1\) Veronese factors and one positive-degree factor.

The paper develops robust tensor-decomposition methods under quantitative nondegeneracy conditions, whereas the present theorem separates exact pointwise finite stopping from impossibility of uniform inference on the qualitative class.

The finite-cumulant-sequence theorem implies that a nondegenerate non-Gaussian law with all moments has infinitely many nonzero higher cumulants, which ensures representation-specific finite stopping but supplies no uniform stopping order.

tldr: A fixed normalized overcomplete-ICA law can support many source-minimal cyclic latent structural completions, yet its ordered equilibrium effect has an exact finite image. The image is the set of source-column ratios whose complementary deletion matrix has full row rank. Necessity follows from intervention solvability; constructive sufficiency uses one latent-row shear and one perfect matching, producing exact same-law countermodels and an \(O(n^4)\) all-witness algorithm. On a separated common-cumulant-order iid class, an explicit tensor-pencil inverse yields simultaneous coverage and root-\(N\) Hausdorff uncertainty for the finite frontier. Heterogeneous source-specific cumulant orders remain a first-class open problem.

project_justification.gap: Published latent cyclic LiNG work characterizes graph-level distributional equivalence or coefficients in a known mixed graph, while published latent acyclic work gives graphical effect criteria. None of these results characterizes the numerical intervention-effect image of every source-minimal cyclic completion of one fixed overcomplete-ICA representation.
project_justification.niche: The fixed-law fiber supplies numerical source directions, so a query-specific algebraic criterion can be both sharper and much smaller than the compatible graph class without imposing dynamical stability.
project_justification.fill: The deletion-rank frontier gives necessary and sufficient attainability, exact witnesses, point-identification and countermodel certificates, polynomial-time enumeration, and a separated iid inference layer with explicit finite-sample coverage.

related_work: DaiAlbrechtSpirtesZhang2026 provides the writing and identification exemplar: its introduction moves from latent cyclic ambiguity to equivalence-class structure, and its main proof converts children bases into perfect matchings; the present target instead fixes one numerical law and projects its completion fiber onto one equilibrium effect. TramontanoKivvaSalehkaleybarDrtonKiyavash2024 motivates query-specific effect identification and proves complete acyclic criteria, while its conclusion leaves cyclic extensions open. TramontanoDrtonEtesami2026 studies coefficient identification for a known mixed graph and obtains only partial cyclic criteria, a different conditioning object from the fixed source-direction fiber. In LacerdaSpirtesRamseyHoyer2008, Section 4 constructs square candidates by admissible row permutations, while Theorem 1 states that LiNG-D returns a distribution-entailment equivalence class. The equality of the candidates' equilibrium-effect projection with \(\mathcal R_{xy}(C)\) is the new square-case reduction here. BongersForrePetersMooij2021 supplies the distinction between observational and interventional solvability. WangSeigal2026 supplies the OICA identification and coupled-decomposition benchmark, AnandkumarGeJanzamin2015 supplies the tensor perturbation technique, and ChenBickel2006 supplies the asymptotic ICA motivation; none studies a rank-selected causal set. PodosinnikovaEtAl2019 and VirtaNordhausenOja2016 inform the heterogeneous-order open question. NandyMaathuisRichardson2017 confirms that joint interventions require globally compatible assignments rather than Cartesian products, motivating but not subsuming the deferred joint-frontier seed.
technical_internal_limitation: Source minimality means exactly one distinct disturbance per structural equation, with no source sharing or splitting, and the fixed-law convention holds one recovered normalized OICA representation fixed while latent rows vary. Enlarging the fiber to split or duplicated sources, graphically irreducible completions, or alternate normalized source representations can change the frontier, so no invariance claim is made for those larger objects. The rank and denominator margins exclude the discontinuity surfaces on which uniform root-\(N\) Hausdorff inference is impossible. The fourteen-stock Hong Kong series is a consumer of the population certificate only: its serial dependence and documented mechanism changes violate the iid inference model unless a separate dependent-time-series theorem and an empirical separation certificate are supplied.
honest_scope: The theorem spine asks for the scalar fixed-law frontier, constructive sharpness, exact countermodels, and iid inference on a nonempty common-order separated class with \(d\ge1\), \(q\ge1\), and \(n\le\binom{p+d-1}{d}\). In the square case, LacerdaSpirtesRamseyHoyer2008 Section 4 supplies admissible row-permutation candidates and its Theorem 1 supplies the distribution-entailment statement; equality of their effect projection with the deletion-rank frontier is the reduction claimed here. Stability-refined completions, common-completion joint intervention matrices, dependent-time-series inference for the Hong Kong data, representation invariance beyond a fixed normalized OICA tuple, and source-specific multi-order recovery are not claimed. The last item is retained as the explicit open-ended question with a concrete coupled-Hessian and multi-cumulant handle.
